- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.61) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.17), model tends to overestimate mean — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — if sentiment drops below -0.30 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period (days 20–30) — apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is weak or negative in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (0.17+) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction to avoid “sentiment inflation” bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows — if forecast is >1.5% above 5-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
